newsitem.title: CHINA: Angang New Steel offers 890 mln H-shares in float.
newsitem.headline: Angang New Steel offers 890 mln H-shares in float.

text.p: Chinese steel producer Angang New Steel Co Ltd said on Monday it is offering 890 million H-shares, or 40.3 percent of the enlarged share capital, at a price ranging from HK$1.61 to HK$1.97 each in a global flotation.
Ten percent of the issue, or 89 million shares, will be offered to the public in Hong Kong.
The remaining 801 million shares will be placed internationally to professional and institutional investors.

The issue price will represent a prospective price to earnings multiple of 7.5 to 9.0 times on a fully-diluted basis and 6.4 to 7.8 times on a weighted average basis, the company said in a listing prospectus.
The adjusted net tangible asset value per share is 1.90 yuan to 2.03 yuan (HK$1.78 to HK$1.90) and the dividend yield is 1.8 percent to 2.2 percent, it said.
H-shares are Chinese enterprises' shares listed in Hong Kong.
The public offering in Hong Kong will run from July 15-18 and the issue price will be fixed on July 19.
Dealing in the shares is expected to begin on July 24 in Hong Kong, it said.
ING Barings is the sponsor, global coordinator and lead manager of the issue.
The Chinese steel producer said it had granted underwriters an option to require it to issue up to a further 77 million H-shares to cover over-subscription and over-allotment.
Angang also said it would issue 300 million A-shares at a price of not less than 4.82 yuan per share.
The A-shares are expected to be listed on the Shenzhen Securities Exchange after the listing of the H-shares in Hong Kong but before October 31, it said.
A-shares are Chinese enterprises' shares listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen, and are only for mainland domestic investors.

The company's parent Angang Holding, a Chinese state-owned enterprise, will hold 52.6 percent of the company following the H-share and A-share offer but before the exercise of the over-allotment option, it said.
Angang produced 891,400 tonnes of cold rolled sheets, 590,600 tonnes of wire rods and 730,500 tonnes of thick plates in the year ended December 31, 1996.
China accounted for 77.6 percent of the total sales for the year, with the rest exported to the United States, South Korea, Japan, Canada, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, it said.
The company said it estimated the H-share issue would raise about HK$1.51 billion, using the mid-range price of HK$1.79 for the calculation.
The A-share issue would raise 1.40 billion yuan, it said.
Angang said the proceeds would be used to build a smelting plant in China and install pickling, rolling, cutting and packaging lines.
Proceeds would also be used to finance its contribution to an equity joint venture for producing galvanised steel and for working capital, it said.

Angang forecast its profit after taxation but before extraordinary items of not less than 480 million yuan for the year ending in December 1997, up from 636 million yuan in 1996, 303 million yuan in 1995 and 605 million yuan in 1994 in accordance with international accounting standards.
Turnover was 6.24 billion yuan in 1996, up from 3.71 billion yuan in 1995 and 4.33 billion yuan in 1994, it said.
Analysts said Angang would be the first H-share to be listed since Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule on July 1.
